What is the Adaptive Spine?

Your Business Has a
Memory Problem

Every day, critical context gets lost between tools. Customer conversations in Slack. Deal status in Salesforce. Support tickets in Zendesk. Billing details in QuickBooks.

The Adaptive Spine solves this by creating a persistent, governed memory layer that unifies everything—so your business can remember, learn, and act with complete context.

Connect Everything.

The Adaptive Spine ingests data from structured systems, unstructured communications, and AI session knowledge—creating a complete picture of your business.

How Ingestion Works

1
Bi-Directional Sync

Data flows both ways. Changes in your CRM update the Spine. Changes approved in the Workbench update your CRM. Always in sync.

2
Real-Time Processing

Every new email, Slack message, or deal update is processed immediately. Your memory stays current, not stale.

3
Semantic Extraction

We don't just store text. We extract intent, entities, relationships, and sentiment—turning raw data into structured knowledge.

4
Deduplication & Merging

Same customer in multiple systems? We merge them into a single entity with complete history. No duplicates, no confusion.

Entity Graph & Memory

From Scattered Data to
Shared Truth

After ingestion, data is normalized into an entity graph—a living map of relationships between people, accounts, projects, and events.

What is the Entity Graph?

It's a knowledge graph that connects every piece of information in your business. Customers link to deals. Deals link to support tickets. Support tickets link to Slack threads. Everything is connected.

Example: Customer 360 View

When you look up "Acme Corp" in the Workbench, you see:

  • All deals (past and present)
  • Every support ticket with sentiment analysis
  • Slack conversations mentioning them
  • Meeting notes and decisions
  • Product usage data and trends
Vector Embeddings

Every entity is vectorized for semantic search. Find similar customers, related issues, or analogous situations instantly.

Temporal Awareness

The graph remembers when things happened. See how relationships evolved over time, not just their current state.

Trust by Design

Governance Boundaries

The Adaptive Spine isn't just smart—it's safe. Every piece of data is governed by strict access controls, audit logs, and approval gates.

Role-Based Access Control

Only see what you're authorized to see. Account managers can't access finance data. Sales can't see engineering roadmaps.

Workspace-level permissions
Entity-level access control
Field-level encryption

Audit Trails

Every action is logged. Who accessed what data, when, and why. Full transparency for compliance and security teams.

Immutable audit logs
Data lineage tracking
Export for compliance

Human-in-the-Loop

AI can suggest. Only humans can approve. No action is taken, no memory is written, without explicit consent.

Approval gates before actions
Review before memory writes
Override AI suggestions

The Four Walls of Trust

1. Separation of Memory & Reasoning

Your data (TruthLayer) is isolated from AI reasoning (Cognitive Shell). Models can be swapped without touching your memory.

2. Workspace Isolation

Private workspaces never leak data. Your personal notes don't mix with company data. Team A can't see Team B's memory.

3. No AI Training on Your Data

We never use your data to train models. Your competitive intelligence stays yours. Period.

4. Approval Before Action

Every suggested action requires human approval. You're always in control. AI assists, you decide.
